# GPU Sandbox Pricing: Modal vs Daytona vs Thunder Compute (2026)

GPU sandbox pricing compared: an H100 sandbox costs $2.95 to $3.95/hr at Thunder Compute, Modal and Daytona. See full per-second rates and real costs.

Carl Peterson · Updated Nov 05, 2026 · 10 min Read

H100 GPU sandboxes start at $2.95/hr on Thunder Compute and cost up to $3.95/hr on Modal and Daytona's on-demand tier. Daytona also offers cheaper preemptible rates, but sandboxes can be terminated without notice. All three platforms charge separately for vCPUs and memory; GPU rates are only part of the bill.

This guide breaks down the GPU sandbox bill and the rules that affect the total. Base prices were last reviewed in October 2026, before volume discounts or region multipliers.

Takeaways

- vCPU and memory add $0.92-1.34/hr to a sandbox for 8 vCPUs and 32 GiB of memory.
- Full configurations at base rates range from $3.20/hr (Daytona preemptible) to $5.29/hr (Modal).
- Per second billing is the standard among covered providers.
- Preemptible GPU sandboxes cost less but can be terminated without notice.
- Modal with narrow region selection costs 2.4x more than Thunder Compute for the example configuration ($9.25/hr vs $3.88/hr).

## What a GPU Sandbox Actually Costs per Hour

A realistic H100 GPU sandbox costs $3.20-$5.29/hr across these options once CPU and memory are included. This cost table prices one H100 with 8 vCPUs, 32 GiB of memory and 100 GiB of storage at list rates.

Three additional items beyond the GPU have an impact on the bill:

- Resources billed on top of the GPU.
- Preemption.
- Egress.

Thunder Compute, Daytona and Modal handle each rule differently.

### CPU, Memory and Storage on Top of the GPU

All three platforms bill GPU, CPU and memory for as long as a sandbox runs. Thunder Compute and Daytona also bill storage; Modal does not bill Sandbox disk separately. On Thunder Compute and Daytona, 8 vCPUs and 32 GiB of memory add $0.92/hr to an H100 sandbox. On Modal, the same resources cost $1.34/hr.

Resource sizing matters as much as the GPU choice. Thunder Compute and Daytona bill the vCPUs and memory you configure. Modal bills whichever is higher, your request or actual usage.

...

Daytona's preemptible GPU rate is about 42% lower than its on-demand rate for every GPU. A Daytona H100 costs $3.95/hr on-demand and $2.27/hr preemptible. Preemptible sandboxes can be terminated without notice, keeping evicted sandboxes retrievable for 24 hours.

...

### Egress: Modal's New Network Charge

Modal started charging for network egress on October 1, 2026. Modal's egress billing charges $0.04/GiB once a workspace uses its allowance for the billing cycle:

- Starter: 1 TiB included
- Team: 10 TiB included
- Enterprise: 100 TiB included

Egress covers traffic leaving a container's network interface, including private traffic to other Modal containers and uploads through Cloud Bucket Mounts. Reads from and writes to Modal Volumes don't count.

...

Default timeouts cap how long an idle sandbox keeps billing:

- Thunder Compute sandboxes expire after 300 seconds by default. This timeout can be extended or disabled.
- Modal Sandboxes default to 5 minutes and can run for up to 24 hours.
- Daytona sandboxes auto-stop after 15 idle minutes by default.

Thunder Compute is the cheapest non-preemptible H100 of the three. On long evals and RL rollouts, an eviction throws away the work already done. A run guaranteed to finish at $2.95/hr can end up cheaper than a lower rate plus reruns, and the gap grows with the eviction rate.

GPU sandbox prices look similar at the headline rate and diverge once CPU, memory, preemption and idle time are added. A typical H100 sandbox costs about $3.88/hr on Thunder Compute, $4.88/hr on Daytona on-demand and $5.29/hr on Modal.

Price the full configuration you plan to run, then weigh what an interrupted run would cost before choosing a preemptible tier.

results.title: Daytona vs Thunder Compute: GPU Sandboxes Compared (2026)
results.author: Carl Peterson
highlights:
Thunder Compute charges a dollar less per non-preemptible H100 hour than Daytona which offers more GPU types, and a spot tier. A non-preemptible H100 costs $2.95/hr on Thunder Compute and $3.95/hr on Daytona's on-demand tier.

Takeaways

- Thunder Compute's non-preemptible H100 costs $2.95/hr, against $3.95/hr on Daytona on-demand.
- A full 8 vCPU, 32 GiB H100 Thunder Compute sandbox costs 20% less ($3.88/hr vs $4.88/hr).
- Daytona spot ($2.27/hr) beats Thunder Compute ($2.95/hr) before factoring in evictions; rerunning preempted work can erase the price gap.

Daytona and Thunder Compute both isolate GPU sandboxes at the VM level and offer capacity that isn't preempted. Details below were verified in October 2026.

## What GPU Rollouts Cost at Scale

If each of 128 parallel rollouts needs its own GPU, a training step costs $68-$113 on H100 sandboxes. That scenario borrows the scale of SWE-MiniSandbox's 128 environments per update, which ran on CPUs. With rollouts capped at 10 minutes, one step uses around 21 GPU-hours, and 100 steps use 2,133 GPU-hours.

The table prices that workload on an H100 sandbox with 8 vCPUs, 32 GiB of memory and 100 GiB of disk at list prices.

| Option | GPU-Hour | Step (128 Rollouts) | 100 Steps |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Thunder Compute | $3.88 | $83 | $8,280 |
| Daytona spot | $3.20 | $68 1 | $6,830 1 |
| Daytona on-demand | $4.88 | $104 | $10,410 |
| Modal | $5.29 | $113 1 | $11,290 1 |
| 1 Before evictions. Every evicted rollout adds the cost of a rerun. | | | |

These rollout costs are an upper bound for one configuration. Rollouts that finish early, CPU-only environments and smaller GPUs all cut the total.

## Running RL Environments on Thunder Compute

Thunder Compute's GPU sandboxes meet RL environment requirements. Each sandbox runs in its own Firecracker microVM (a lightweight, hardware-isolated VM) with a GPU.

### Non-Preemptible H100 and A100 Sandboxes

Thunder Compute sandboxes are never preempted, so a rollout that starts finishes at the quoted price. H100 sandboxes start at $2.95/hr and A100 80GB sandboxes at $1.95/hr, which suits lighter reward models. Thunder Compute charges no region multipliers or egress fees.

How coding-agent evals like SWE-bench run in parallel GPU sandboxes: HumanEval vs SWE-bench, when evals need a GPU, preemption and cost per run.

Carl Peterson · Updated Oct 16, 2026 · 9 min Read

Coding-agent evals run benchmark tasks in isolated sandboxes. They do so in parallel to cut a full run from days to hours. These coding-agents edit real repositories and execute commands, making isolation a security requirement.

...

## What a SWE-bench Eval Run Costs

A full SWE-bench Lite run costs about $160-$265 on H100 GPU sandboxes at list prices. At 300 tasks and about 10 minutes each, one run uses roughly 50 GPU-hours. The table prices that run on an H100 sandbox with 8 vCPUs, 32 GiB of memory and 100 GiB of disk.

| Option | Per Hour | SWE-bench Lite Run (50 GPU-Hours) | 10 Runs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Daytona spot | $3.20 | $160 1 | $1,600 1 |
| Thunder Compute | $3.88 | $194 | $1,940 |
| Daytona on-demand | $4.88 | $244 | $2,440 |
| Modal | $5.29 | $265 1 | $2,650 1 |

These eval costs assume a GPU in every task sandbox for the full 10 minutes. Tasks that finish early, a shared inference server or a smaller GPU all lower the total.

## Running Coding-Agent Evals on Thunder Compute

Thunder Compute's GPU sandboxes provide ephemeral, API-created environments running in their own Firecracker microVM (a lightweight, hardware-isolated VM) with a GPU attached.

Thunder Compute sandboxes are never preempted, so a task that starts finishes, and pass rates carry no hidden retries. H100 sandboxes cost $2.95/hr, $1/hr below Daytona's on-demand H100. A100 80GB sandboxes cost $1.95/hr for smaller models under test, with no region multipliers or egress fees.

By default, Thunder Compute commands run as durable jobs that survive client disconnects. A dropped connection on the machine driving the eval doesn't end the run. Each sandbox has one GPU, which fits models that run on a single 80 GB card; larger models under test belong on a shared inference server.

# Best GPU Sandboxes for AI Agents (2026)

Compare the best GPU sandboxes for AI agents in 2026. Thunder Compute, Daytona and Modal ranked on GPU types, preemption, isolation and H100 price.

Carl Peterson · Updated Oct 07, 2026 · 7 min Read

The best GPU sandboxes for AI agents in 2026 are Thunder Compute, Daytona and Modal. Thunder Compute offers the lowest on-demand H100 rate of the three. Daytona offers flexible hardware and cheaper spot capacity. Modal has the widest GPU range, from T4 to B300, on a broader serverless platform.

Most agent sandboxes are CPU-only, and only a few sandbox platforms put a GPU inside the sandbox itself. This guide compares three managed GPU sandbox platforms, with verified prices and limits.

Takeaways

- Thunder Compute offers the cheapest non-preemptible H100 sandbox of the three, at $2.95/hr.
- Daytona offers the most flexibility, with eight GPU types and spot capacity.
- Modal has the widest GPU range, from T4 to B300, but its GPU sandboxes are preemptible only.
- E2B and Vercel Sandbox are CPU-only, so they don't qualify as GPU sandboxes.

...

## 1. Thunder Compute: Non-Preemptible H100s at the Lowest On-Demand Rate

Thunder Compute offers the cheapest non-preemptible H100 sandbox of the three, at $2.95/hr against $3.95/hr at Modal and Daytona on-demand. Every Thunder Compute sandbox is non-preemptible. Long evals and RL runs finish at the quoted price instead of being evicted and rerun.

Each Thunder Compute sandbox is a Firecracker microVM (a lightweight, hardware-isolated VM). Sandboxes are created through a Python SDK. Commands run as durable jobs, and outbound network access can be open, blocked or restricted to allowlists.

Best for: long evals, RL rollouts and inference loops where interruptions are costly.

results.title: What Are GPU Sandboxes? How Isolation Works When Agents Need a GPU (2026)
results.author: Carl Peterson
highlights:
Carl Peterson · Updated Oct 07, 2026 · 11 min Read

A GPU sandbox is an isolated environment that gives code a real GPU without exposing the host. Isolation serves two purposes: it contains untrusted code, and it gives every reinforcement learning (RL) or eval rollout a clean, reproducible environment. Most AI sandbox platforms are CPU-only, because the isolation technology many of them use can't hand a GPU to a workload. Three managed platforms offer GPU sandboxes today: Thunder Compute, Modal and Daytona.

...

- GPU sandboxes give untrusted, agent-generated code a real GPU behind an isolation boundary.
- Most AI sandboxes are CPU-only, because stock Firecracker doesn't support GPU passthrough.
- Three isolation paths exist: VFIO passthrough (Daytona), gVisor (Modal) and Firecracker microVMs with custom GPU support (Thunder Compute).
- Preemption, GPU range and persistence separate the three managed GPU sandbox platforms.
- Thunder Compute's H100 sandboxes cost $2.95/hr and are never preempted.

...

### Non-Preemptible GPU Sandboxes with H100s at $2.95 per Hour

Thunder Compute's H100 sandboxes cost $2.95 per hour, billed per second. An H100 costs $3.95/hr at Modal and as an on-demand H100 at Daytona. Every Thunder Compute sandbox is non-preemptible, so long evals and RL runs aren't evicted partway through.

...

Which Platforms Offer GPU Sandboxes in 2026?

Thunder Compute, Modal and Daytona offer managed GPU sandboxes as of October 2026. Beam and NVIDIA OpenShell also support GPUs in sandboxed environments.
